title: Big Three Dragons: Molecular Gas in a Bright Lyman-break Galaxy at z = 7.15
question: Investigate the nature and mass of the molecular gas in the bright Lyman-break galaxy B14-65666 at z = 7.1520 using ALMA Band 3 observations of CO(6-5), CO(7-6), and [CI](2-1) and multiwavelength constraints.

data.sensitivity: Continuum: 4.6 uJy/beam (5.3 uJy/beam tapered); CO(6-5): 96 uJy/beam (107 uJy/beam tapered) per 50 km/s; CO(7-6) and [CI](2-1): 78 uJy/beam (93 uJy/beam tapered) per 50 km/s

what.value: [OIII] 88 um and [CII] 158 um luminosities, spectroscopic redshift z = 7.1520 ± 0.0003, SFR, stellar mass, metallicity, and dynamical mass

evidence.quote: With a stellar mass obtained from SED fitting (M∗ = 7.7+1.0−0.8 × 108 M⊙; Hashimoto et al. 2019)

what.value: Total-infrared luminosity L_TIR and dust mass log(M_dust/M_sun) ≈ 6.4 - 7.5

evidence.quote: Combined with the dust mass of the target, log(Mdust/M∗) ≈ 6.4 − 7.5 (Sugahara et al. 2021)

what.value: Local SFGs, AGNs, and U/LIRGs observed with Herschel/SPIRE

evidence.quote: Small open circles show a compilation of local objects, including SFGs, AGNs, and U/LIRGs observed with Herschel/SPIRE (Kamenetzky et al. 2016)

what.value: Observed and IllustrisTNG volume number density of z ~ 3-4 passive galaxies

evidence.quote: The observed number density of z ∼ 3 − 4 passive galaxies was recently compiled by Valentino et al. (2020); it is O(10−6) −O(10−5) Mpc−3 at M∗ ≥ 4 × 1010 M⊙.

recipe.goal: Create continuum and line cubes and measure upper limits on continuum and line fluxes
recipe.method: Image continuum and 50 km/s spectral cubes with natural weighting and uv-tapering (0.40''-0.45''), integrate cubes over -200 to +200 km/s with CASA immoments to produce moment 0 maps, extract spectra in a 1.5'' diameter aperture, and measure 3-sigma upper limits.
assumptions: CO emitting region size does not exceed that of [CII] emission (covered by the uv-tapered beam)

recipe.goal: Correct line fluxes for CMB and calculate line luminosity upper limits
recipe.method: Apply CMB correction factor f_CMB using da Cunha et al. (2013) Eq. 32 and convert velocity-integrated flux limits to L_line and L'_line using Solomon et al. (1992) formulas.
assumptions: LambdaCDM cosmology with Omega_m = 0.272, Omega_b = 0.045, Omega_Lambda = 0.728, H_0 = 70.4 km s^-1 Mpc^-1

recipe.goal: Estimate molecular gas mass using five independent techniques
recipe.method: Calculate M_mol from (1) mid-J CO upper limits with excitation and metallicity-dependent alpha_CO, (2) [CI](2-1) upper limit with partition function and carbon abundance, (3) [CII] 158 um luminosity with Madden et al. (2020) relation, (4) dust mass and metallicity-dependent DGR, and (5) dynamical mass minus stellar mass.
key_parameters: alpha_CO = 25 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1 (range 5 - 25 for Z = 0.2 - 0.8 Z_sun)
assumptions: X[CI]/X[H2] ~ 1.6 x 10^-5 (and up to 10x higher conversion factor at low Z)
HII region contribution to [CII] is ~30% and CMB attenuation factor for [CII] is f_CMB = 0.5 - 1.0
Gas is predominantly in the molecular phase for the dust-based estimate

recipe.goal: Constrain PDR gas density and FUV radiation field using PDR Toolbox
recipe.method: Compare observed L_[CII]/L_FIR, L_[CII]/L_CO(6-5), L_[CII]/L_CO(7-6), and L_[CII]/L_[CI](2-1) ratios against PDR Toolbox (version wk2020) model grids to constrain hydrogen nuclei density n(H) and incident FUV field G.
assumptions: Divide optically thin emission luminosities by a factor of 2 for spherical cloud geometry; PDR fraction of [CII] is 70%

recipe.goal: Compute molecular gas fraction and gas depletion time
recipe.method: Divide the derived M_mol range by SFR and stellar mass from SED fitting to obtain tau_dep and mu_gas, and compare with high-z literature samples and scaling relations.
